newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-DORTMUND SAYS RIEDLE MOVE TO LIVERPOOL SEALED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DORTMUND SAYS RIEDLE MOVE TO LIVERPOOL SEALED.

text.p: Liverpool look to have beaten off English premier league rivals Newcastle in the chase for Borussia Dortmund striker Karl-Heinz Riedle, the German club said on Wednesday.
"The clubs are agreed. Only the signature is outstanding," Dortmund spokesman Josef Schneck told the German SID agency.
Dortmund's sports director Ottmar Hitzfeld, who guided the Germans to a 3-1 European Cup final win over Juventus in May, said earlier: "The deal with Liverpool is just about done.
"Nothing will actually happen today -- but tomorrow or the day after could be different."
Liverpool denied an interest in Riedle earlier this week, despite Hitzfeld claiming an approach had been made, but look now to be close to clinching the signing.
According to press reports, the 31-year-old Riedle -- who scored twice in the Champions' League final -- will sign a 1.8-million-pound ($2.9-million) three-year deal.
German media reports said the striker would be paid an annual salary of 3.7 million marks ($2 million) under the agreement.

Newcastle boss Kenny Dalglish is believed to have wanted Riedle as a short-term replacement for the injured Alan Shearer while Liverpool manager Roy Evans wants the German to replace Stan Collymore who left Anfield for Aston Villa in a seven-million-pound ($11.7-million) deal.
Dortmund's new coach Nevio Scala backed the move.
"If he wants to go then he should. We can't hold him back from such a chance," he said, adding that Dortmund would then be on the look out for a new striker.

German media reports said Riedle's wife had already been house hunting in the English north-western city with Evans and had found something in the Southport area, where former Dortmund team mate Patrik Berger, who joined Liverpool last year, also lives.
